papers.title: SYNTHETIC CONTROL: A blocked high-resolution Aurora simulation

sections.heading: Attempt and limitation
sections.text: Tracking all pairwise couplings in the Aurora simulator exceeded the memory of available hardware, so our high-resolution simulation attempt failed. High-resolution simulation would let us distinguish two competing mechanisms for extreme events, which our current coarse model cannot separate. The dense interaction representation is the specific memory bottleneck; simply collecting more observations does not remove it.

sections.heading: New capability and unresolved validation
sections.text: SpectraSparse stores only significant interaction blocks and reduces memory use while preserving aggregate coupling statistics in small systems. Its behavior for rare, high-amplitude events and large high-resolution simulations remains untested. This method has not yet been evaluated in the Aurora simulator. Whether sparse storage can remove Aurora's memory bottleneck without losing its extreme-event behavior is an open experimental question.
